reason: Comparison with the Nuremberg copy corrected the catalogue's 'oppositio ampliationis' to 'opposita amplia-/tioni' and the first reading's 'distinctionem desctrictionem' to 'diffinitionem restrictionis', and showed that the underlined words are lemmata in a divisio textus.
sources: Nuremberg, Germanisches Nationalmuseum, Hs 27773, fol. 128ra-rb, Compilationes supra Summulas Petri Hispani, page image dlib.gnm.de/item/Hs27773/258

L. M. de Rijk, 'On the Genuine Text of Peter of Spain's Summule logicales (Conclusion). V', Vivarium 8 (1970), pp. 30-37: manuscripts (pp. 31-32, Vienna 2389 interpolated p. 32), incipit 'Omnes homines' (p. 33), twelve-tract order (p. 36), no clue to origin or author (p. 37)
L. M. de Rijk (ed.), Peter of Spain, Tractatus called afterwards Summule logicales (Assen 1972), IX De ampliationibus p. 194, X De appellationibus p. 197, XI De restrictionibus pp. 204 and 207
L. M. de Rijk, Vivarium 7 (1969), p. 135: Guillelmus Arnaldi, Lectura tractatuum, openings of the ampliation and appellation lectiones (rejected)

SOURCE-ASSISTED READING of F-kcu7 (Wien, ÖNB, Cod. 3637, guard strips), made after comparison with the anonymous Compilationes supra Summulas Petri Hispani ("Omnes homines"), Nuremberg, Germanisches Nationalmuseum, Hs 27773, fol. 128ra-rb (page image). Lines reread on the image by a research reader: the whole visible column of the front strip (canvas 0, about 1420,1100-2620,2900) and of the back strip (canvas 1, rotated 180 degrees, about 260,1000-1480,3000). Lines under the leather turn-ins are unread. ( ) = expansion, [ ] = lost, abraded or supplied, ? = uncertain, *...* = lemma underlined in the manuscript.
